title: The prostration
hookLine: forehead on the ground, glory to my Lord the Most High, the closest a person gets

lines: ON THE GROUND YOU WALK ON.
cards: Knees, then hands, then the forehead on the floor. The highest part of a person, the part with the face and the mind in it, placed on the same ground you walk on. In a wrestling match, ending up face-down is losing.
In the prayer, it's the moment of nearness. Every day this week the body has gone a little lower. Now it goes all the way down.

teach.h: SUJUD — THE MASJID IS NAMED FOR IT.
teach.b: The word is sujud, prostration. The same root gives masjid, the Arabic word behind mosque: the place of prostration. The whole building is named for this one moment.
A hadith in Bukhari says it's done on seven bones: the forehead, with the nose; the two hands; the two knees; and the toes of both feet.
Seven points of the body touching the earth, and every unit of the prayer has two prostrations. There, usually three times, the person says: subhana rabbiya al-a'la.

teach.h: GLORY TO MY LORD, THE MOST HIGH.
teach.b: Glory to my Lord, the Most High. Notice the pairing. In the bow, you said the Great.
Now, at the lowest point your body can reach, you say the Most High. The lower you go, the higher the name. Then the hadith that gives today its line, in Sahih Muslim.
The Prophet ﷺ said: the closest a servant is to his Lord is while prostrating, so make much supplication there. Not standing tall. Not at the head of a line.
Face on the floor. The hadith points there for a person's own requests, said silently.
Surah al-Alaq, the surah that begins with Read, ends on the same idea: prostrate yourself, and draw near. In the hadith, the lowest point is the nearest.

how: In each unit of prayer, Muslims prostrate twice on seven points (forehead and nose, hands, knees, toes), usually saying subhana rabbiya al-a'la three times, and some add their own supplications there silently.

o: sitting cross-legged to share a meal
prostration, the forehead placed on the ground
lying flat on the floor with arms spread out

games.q: what's inside the prostration — tap the pairs.

s: the word mosque, masjid, means the place of prostration
it comes from the same root as sujud.
prostration is done on the forehead alone
the hadith says seven bones: forehead with nose, both hands, both knees, both feet.
a hadith says a person is closest to God while prostrating
it's in Sahih Muslim: so make much supplication there.

games.q: you're in the prayer and want to ask God for something personal, in your own words. where does the hadith point you?
o: only after the prayer is over
games.why: the closest a servant is to his Lord is while prostrating, so make much supplication there (Muslim).

practice: If your body allows, kneel, place your hands flat on the floor, and lower your forehead and nose to the ground; if it doesn't, sit and bow your head as low as is comfortable, and that counts too.
Stay there, and feel the seven points, or however many are touching. If you pray, you can say subhana rabbiya al-a'la three times, then ask for one thing in your own words, and rest there.

wordCard.voice: Sujud. Prostration: forehead on the ground, glory to my Lord the Most High, the closest a person gets. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: prostration. The same root gives masjid (مَسْجِد), the place of prostration.

carryVoice: Your line: closest when lowest. Brought low, in the tradition's hearing, might be the closest place. A week of the prayer, done.

sources.ref: Sahih Muslim 482 (the closest a servant is to his Lord is while prostrating)
Sahih Muslim 772 (subhana rabbiya al-a'la in prostration)
